subject: PED
label: Grade 12 Commerce
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 12 Commerce Physical education, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 2 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Physical education and sports for all
modules.outcome: plan inclusive sport and fitness programmes
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Physical education and sports for all', you learn to plan inclusive sport and fitness programmes. You work with exam-style questions and written reasoning. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Place it: find where and when 'Physical education and sports for all' happens, on a map, a timeline or in a local example.
Gather: read or listen to two short sources and note who is speaking and why.
Use it: plan inclusive sport and fitness programmes. Give a reason and one piece of evidence for every point.
Weigh it: say what another person might think, and why, before you decide.
modules.example: Solved: Fitness check: resting pulse, one-minute step test, record, repeat after 4 weeks. FITT: frequency, intensity, time, type. Method: Model run for 'Physical education and sports for all'. Question: what happened, or what is the situation, and why? Sources: two short extracts, a map or table. Notes: who, what, where, when, why. Answer: three sentences, each with a reason and a piece of evidence. Check: is there a point of view that you have not considered? What a good answer looks like: facts are correct, reasons are linked to evidence, and one other point of view is named fairly.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Plan inclusive sport and fitness programmes: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.
steps: Step 1, Define sports for all: opportunity for every person, whatever age, gender, ability or income, to take part. Children with special needs include those with visual, hearing, movement or learning differences. The Paralympics began in Rome in 1960.

Step 2, Plan a school sports day for 200 students, 12 of whom have disabilities. Offer three stations: wheelchair relay, goalball for visually impaired players, and sitting volleyball. Inclusive design offers modified rules so all play together.

Step 3, Check the venue. A ramp rising 0.5 m at a slope of 1 in 12 must be 0.5 x 12 = 6 m long. Also keep clear paths, shaded seating, drinking water and a quiet area. Provide large-print or audio instructions as needed.

Step 4, Plan a 45-minute session: warm-up 10 minutes, skill practice 20 minutes, small-sided game 10 minutes, cool-down 5 minutes. Total 10 + 20 + 10 + 5 = 45. Pair students of different abilities, using the same equipment with adapted rules.

Step 5, Write a model aim: 'Raise activity so every student reaches 60 minutes of movement on at least three days a week, tracked with a simple tally sheet. Review after 12 weeks and adjust equipment or rules where students are left out.'

Step 6, Your turn: suggest two ways to include a girls-only afternoon and a student using crutches. Model answer: 'Offer a girls session with female coaches, and give the crutch user roles such as scorer or a seated throwing game.'

modules.title: Training, nutrition and sports injuries
modules.outcome: describe training methods, balanced diet and first aid for injuries
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Training, nutrition and sports injuries', you learn to describe training methods, balanced diet and first aid for injuries. You work with exam-style questions and written reasoning. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Place it: find where and when 'Training, nutrition and sports injuries' happens, on a map, a timeline or in a local example.
Gather: read or listen to two short sources and note who is speaking and why.
Use it: describe training methods, balanced diet and first aid for injuries. Give a reason and one piece of evidence for every point.
Weigh it: say what another person might think, and why, before you decide.
modules.example: Solved: Fitness check: resting pulse, one-minute step test, record, repeat after 4 weeks. FITT: frequency, intensity, time, type. Method: Model run for 'Training, nutrition and sports injuries'. Question: what happened, or what is the situation, and why? Sources: two short extracts, a map or table. Notes: who, what, where, when, why. Answer: three sentences, each with a reason and a piece of evidence. Check: is there a point of view that you have not considered? What a good answer looks like: facts are correct, reasons are linked to evidence, and one other point of view is named fairly.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Describe training methods, balanced diet and first aid for injuries: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.
steps: Step 1, Compare training methods. Continuous running builds endurance, such as 30 minutes at steady pace. Interval training alternates work and rest, such as 6 x 200 m at 80 percent effort with 90 seconds rest. Fartlek mixes fast and slow. Circuit training rotates stations.

Step 2, Apply progressive overload. A runner jogs 20 minutes at week 1 and adds about 10 percent each week: 22 min, 24 min, 27 min. Increases must be gradual to avoid injury, and recovery days let muscles repair and grow stronger.

Step 3, Calculate energy. Carbohydrate and protein give 4 kcal per gram and fat 9. A meal with 100 g carbohydrate, 30 g protein and 20 g fat gives 400 + 120 + 180 = 700 kcal, with about 57 percent from carbohydrate.

Step 4, Balance a plate for an athlete: whole grains and fruit for carbohydrate, eggs, pulses or fish for protein, a little oil or nuts for fat, vegetables for vitamins and fibre, plus water before, during and after training.

Step 5, Give first aid for an ankle sprain with PRICE: protect, rest, ice for 15 to 20 minutes every few hours, compression with a bandage and elevation above heart level. Seek medical help if the foot cannot bear weight, which may mean a fracture.

Step 6, Your turn: a sprinter pulls a hamstring muscle. Name the injury type and give first aid. Model answer: 'It is a strain. Stop, rest, ice, compress and elevate, then see a physiotherapist before returning.'

L2: read maps and timelines; describe local government and history.
L4: analyse causes and consequences; argue from evidence.
